posts.name: Amitabha
posts.cooked:
why echo https://www.example.com/page1 | cut -d/ -f3 | grep -v 'WWW\.'
is matching full www.example.com not only www.
If I make grep -E 'WWW\.' why it is not selecting anything

posts.name: Amitabha
posts.cooked:
Got it
I some how confused between -v and -o

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
Few things

  1. As you mentioned, -v is for inverse matching, whereas -o is for printing only the match
  2. Grep is case sensitive. WWW won’t match www. It prints for -v exactly due to this, as it doesn’t match.

posts.name: Amitabha
posts.cooked: cut -d/ f2 why it return nothing or empty string

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
cut -d/ -f2 is not returning empty string. It is returning the domain name.

The grep is removing all rows which does not match.

Remove the grep from command to confirm.

posts.name: Amitabha
posts.cooked:
image801×139 22.3 KB

This is what I get , Am I missing something?

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
My bad, I misread -f2 as -f3.

Yes it expected to be empty cause there is nothing between the first and second slash

posts.name: Amitabha
posts.cooked:
image1075×766 86.5 KB

second question
grep -v “(WWW\.)” ------ produce the same effect ?
If yes then what is the difference?

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
1. yes, it ignores all the lines that have www in the domain.
  2. No, as i mentioned grep is case sensitive.

posts.name: Amitabha
posts.cooked:
thanks for clarifying the doubt

I have only one question left
grep -v “(www.)” and grep -v ‘www.’

Are there any difference on result?
MY question is why you choose ‘www.’ but not not “(www.)”:
Also confuse when we use ’ ’ and when " "

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
If using -E then they are same.
Otherwise it matches a literal pair of parentheses. You can use \( and \) to escape them, again, then they are same.

It is used for grouping the expression, please go through navigating linux 6.3.6 to understand how grouping works and how it is used in back-references.

Amitabhab:

Also confuse when we use ’ ’ and when " "

This has nothing to do with grep, this is how bash works. Variables are expanded inside " " so we stick to ' ' so that all strings are passed as is to grep.
